This parameter is required when sending a message to a device that uses the cloud gateway GB/T 32960 protocol. It specifies the command type of the message. Valid values:
- **128**: Query command (0x80).
- **129**: Set command (0x81).
- **130**: In-vehicle terminal control command (0x82).

For more information about connecting devices that use the cloud gateway GB/T 32960 protocol, see [Overview of the Cloud Gateway GB/T 32960 Protocol](~~2248990~~).

You must convert the original message into binary data and then encode it in Base64 to generate the message body.

When sending a message to a device that uses the MQTT protocol, you must specify the custom topic of the corresponding device. The operation permission of the topic must be **subscribe** or **publish and subscribe**.

When sending a message to a device that uses the GB/T 32960 protocol via a cloud gateway, you do not need to specify this parameter.

Sign.description:
The signature of the sub-device.

Set the Sign parameter to the result of the **SignMethod(deviceSecret,content)** function.

To obtain the **content** parameter, sort all sub-device parameters that are submitted to the server, except the Sign and SignMethod parameters, in alphabetical order. Then, concatenate the parameters and values in sequence. No concatenation symbol is required to separate these parameters and values.

For example, you want to specify the following parameters for a sub-device: **ClientId=868575026974305, DeviceName=868575026974305, ProductKey=a1PB5fp1234, SignMethod=hmacmd5, timestamp=1646277090411, and deviceSecret=1234**. In this case, the signature function is `hmacmd5(1234, clientId868575026974305deviceName868575026974305productKeya1PB5fp1234timestamp1646277090411)`, and the calculation result is `3BA0DFA4C477B40C007D84D30D6466CC`.

>  In the preceding example, **ClientId** indicates the client ID of the sub-device. You can specify a custom client ID.

For more information about how to calculate the signature value, see [How do I obtain MQTT parameters for authentication?](~~292635~~). The signature value is the calculated value of the passwd parameter.

Timestamp.description:
The timestamp in UTC. This parameter is optional.

> If this parameter is included in the value of the **TopoAddItem.N.Sign** parameter, you must specify this parameter.

SignMethod.description: The signature algorithm. Valid values: **hmacSha1**, **hmacSha256**, **hmacMd5**, and **Sha256**. The value is not case-sensitive.

ClientId.description:
The client ID of the sub-device. The ID can be the serial number (SN) or media access control (MAC) address of the device. This parameter is optional.

> If this parameter is included in the value of the **TopoAddItem.N.Sign** parameter, you must specify this parameter.

BatchAddThingTopo.title: BatchAddThingTopo
BatchAddThingTopo.summary: Invoke this API to batch add device topology relationships.
BatchAddThingTopo.description:
## How-To

- You can add up to 10 sub-devices to a gateway in a single API call.

- The API caller must be the owner of the gateway.

- Each Alibaba Cloud account is limited to 5 queries per second (QPS) when calling this API.

- If a sub-device passed in already has an existing topology relationship, its original gateway will be replaced with the current gateway.

- If the topology relationship between any sub-device and the gateway fails to be established, the system performs a rollback, and the topology relationships between all passed-in sub-devices and the current gateway fail to be established.

## QPS Limit
Each Alibaba Cloud account can send a maximum of 10 requests per second (QPS) to this API.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

BatchCheckDeviceNames.title: BatchCheckDeviceNames
BatchCheckDeviceNames.summary: Call this API to batch customize device names under a specified product. The IoT Platform validates the legitimacy of the names.
BatchCheckDeviceNames.description:
## How-To

Use this API together with the **BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId** API to register multiple devices under one product and assign a unique name to each device.

The batch device registration flow is as follows:

1. Call this API and pass the names of the devices you want to register in batch. The IoT Platform returns an application batch ID (**ApplyId**). A successful response indicates that the request to validate the device names in batch has been successfully submitted. The actual validation is executed asynchronously and takes some time.
2. Call [QueryBatchRegisterDeviceStatus](~~69483~~) to view the result of the name validation.
3. Call [BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId](~~69514~~) to register the devices in batch.
4. (Optional) Call [QueryBatchRegisterDeviceStatus](~~69483~~) to check the device registration result.
5. Call [QueryPageByApplyId](~~69518~~) to view the information of the registered devices.

## Limits

You can define up to 10,000 device names in a single call.

## QPS Limit

Each Alibaba Cloud account can make a maximum of 10 queries per second (QPS) to this API.

> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

## How-To  
During instance migration, if new devices have not undergone grayscale migration, you can call this API to continuously migrate incremental devices in grayscale mode.  

Before calling this API, you must have created a grayscale migration job in the [IoT Platform console](https://iot.console.aliyun.com/), completed grayscale verification, and ensured that the job is already in the grayscale-completed status. You can use one of the following methods to register multiple devices:

*   If you want to generate random DeviceNames, call the BatchRegisterDevice operation.

    Perform the following steps to register devices and view the result:

    1\. Call the BatchRegisterDevice operation to register multiple devices. A successful response indicates that the registration request is submitted. The actual registration process is asynchronously implemented and takes some minutes.

    2\. Call the [QueryBatchRegisterDeviceStatus](~~69483~~) operation to query the device registration result.

    3\. Call the [QueryPageByApplyId](~~69518~~) operation to view the details of registered devices. The details include the DeviceName, DeviceSecret, and IotId parameters.

*   If you want to specify custom DeviceNames, call the BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId operation. For more information, see [BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId](~~69514~~).

## Limits

- You can create a maximum of 10,000 devices in a single call.
- Each Alibaba Cloud account can run a maximum of 10 queries per second (QPS).  >  RAM users of an Alibaba Cloud account share the quota of the account.

BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId.description:
You can use one of the following methods to register multiple devices at a time:

*   Call the [BatchRegisterDevice](~~69473~~) operation to generate random DeviceNames.

*   Call the BatchRegisterDeviceWithApplyId and **BatchCheckDeviceNames** operations to specify custom DeviceNames. Procedure:

>  If your instance has an ID, you must specify this parameter. Otherwise, the request fails. If no Overview page exists or no instance ID is displayed, you do not need to specify this parameter.

DataSource ID.

The topic that you want to add to the data source in the rules engine. Format: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/topicShortName`. `${productKey}` specifies the **ProductKey** of the product to which a device belongs. `${deviceName}` specifies the name of the device. `topicShortName` specifies the custom name of the topic.

*   Basic communication topics or Thing Specification Language (TSL) communication topics are in the `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/topicShortName` format. You can replace `${deviceName}` with the plus sign (`+`) wildcard character. The wildcard character specifies that the topic applies to all devices in the product. Valid values of `topicShortName`:

    *   `/thing/event/property/post`: submits the property data of a device.
    *   `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: submits the event data of a device. `${tsl.event.identifier}` specifies the identifier of an event in the TSL model.
    *   `/thing/lifecycle`: submits device lifecycle changes.
    *   `/thing/downlink/reply/message`: sends a response to a request from IoT Platform.
    *   `/thing/list/found`: submits data when a gateway detects a new sub-device.
    *   `/thing/topo/lifecycle`: submits device topology changes.
    *   `/thing/event/property/history/post`: submits the historical property data of a device.
    *   `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: submits the historical event data of a device. `${tsl.event.identifier}` specifies the identifier of an event in the TSL model.
    *   `/ota/upgrade`: submits the over-the-air (OTA) update status.
    *   `/ota/version/post`: submits OTA module versions.
    *   `/thing/deviceinfo/update`: submits device tag changes.

    `/${productKey}/${packageId}/${jobId}/ota/job/status`: submits the status of each OTA update batch. This topic is a basic communication topic. `${packageId}` specifies the ID of the update package. `${jobId}` specifies the ID of the update batch.

*   Custom topics are in the `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/user/#` format. Example: `/${productKey}/${deviceName}/user/get`.

    You can call the [QueryProductTopic](~~69647~~) operation to view all custom topics of a product.

    When you specify a custom topic, you can use the plus sign (`+`) and number sign (`#`) wildcard characters.

    *   You can replace `${deviceName}` with the plus sign (`+`) wildcard character. The wildcard character specifies that the topic applies to all devices in the product.
    *   You can replace the fields that follow ${deviceName} with `/user/#`. The number sign (`#`) wildcard character specifies that the topic applies to all fields that follow `/user`.

*   Topics that are used to submit device status changes are in the `/as/mqtt/status/${productKey}/${deviceName}` format.

You can use the plus sign (`+`) wildcard character to specify that the status changes of all devices in the product are submitted.

For more information about how to use wildcard characters, see the "Custom topics with wildcard characters" section in [Use custom topics](~~85539~~).

For more information about the data formats of topics, see [Data formats](~~73736~~).

> You can add only the following topics to the data source in the rules engine for MQTT gateways, devices of MQTT gateways, and products and devices that use the open source MQTT protocol: custom topics, topics that are used to submit device status changes, and topics that are used to submit device lifecycle changes. For more information about custom topics, see the "Messaging" topic. If you set this parameter to a custom topic, you must specify ScopeType and ProductKey. If you set ScopeType to DEVICE, you must specify DeviceName.

The **ProductKey** of the product to which the custom message **topic** belongs.

><notice>You must set this parameter for open-source MQTT hosted products and devices, and for MQTT cloud gateway products and devices.
></notice>

The **device name** of the device to which the custom message **topic** belongs.

><notice>When the **topic** is a custom message **topic** and **scopeType** is **DEVICE**, you must set this parameter for open-source MQTT hosted products and devices, and for MQTT cloud gateway products and devices.

- **PRODUCT**: Product dimension. This value indicates that the subscription applies to all devices under the product. In this case, you must also specify **ProductKey**.
- **DEVICE**: Device dimension. This value indicates that the subscription applies to a specified device under the product. In this case, you must also specify **DeviceName**.

><notice>For open-source MQTT-hosted products and devices, and MQTT cloud gateway products and devices, if the **topic** is a custom message topic, you must specify this parameter.
></notice>

The operation type of the data destination. Valid values:

- **REPUBLISH**: Forward the topic data processed by the resolver script to another communication topic in the IoT Platform.
- **AMQP**: Forward the topic data processed by the resolver script to an AMQP consumer group.
- **DATAHUB**: Forward the topic data processed by the resolver script to Alibaba Cloud DataHub for stream data processing.
- **ONS**: Forward the topic data processed by the resolver script to Alibaba Cloud Message Queue for Apache RocketMQ for message distribution.
- **MNS**: Send the topic data processed by the resolver script to Alibaba Cloud Message Service for message transmission.
- **FC**: Send the topic data processed by the resolver script to Alibaba Cloud Function Compute for event-driven computing.
- **OTS**: Send the topic data processed by the resolver script to Alibaba Cloud Tablestore for NoSQL data storage.

CreateDeviceDistributeJob.title: CreateDeviceDistributeJob
CreateDeviceDistributeJob.summary: Invoke this API to create a device distribution job. By default, the product to which the devices belong is also distributed.
CreateDeviceDistributeJob.description:
## How-To

Follow these steps to complete device distribution.

1. Invoke this API to initiate an asynchronous device distribution job and obtain the **JobId** from the response.

2. Use the **JobId** obtained in the previous step as a request parameter and repeatedly invoke the [QueryDeviceDistributeJob](~~199536~~) API to check the **Status** in the response.

    > You must control the frequency of repeated API calls according to the queries per second (QPS) limit of the API.

    The following **Status** values indicate that the distribution job has reached its desired state:
    - **2**: The device distribution job completed successfully. However, this does not guarantee that all devices were distributed successfully. To obtain the specific result for each device, proceed to the next step.
    - **3**: The distribution job was abnormally interrupted. After handling the abnormal flow, you can re-initiate the device distribution job.

3. Use the **JobId** from step 1 as a request parameter and invoke the [QueryDeviceDistributeDetail](~~199533~~) API to retrieve the **File** parameter, which contains the URL to the distribution result file.

    > The URL to the file is valid for 10 minutes.

4. Access the distribution result details via the file URL. Each device has a corresponding **Code** indicating its distribution result. If **Code** is 200, the device was distributed successfully.

    If a device fails to be distributed, you can repeat the above steps to redistribute it.

## Limitations

- The **Endpoint** for accessing Alibaba Cloud services supports only China (Shanghai), i.e., `iot.cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com`.

- This API does not support creating cross-account distribution jobs.

- A single Alibaba Cloud account can have no more than 10 combined product and device distribution jobs. For information about creating a product distribution job, see [CreateProductDistributeJob](~~199383~~).

- The maximum queries per second (QPS) for invoking this API under a single Alibaba Cloud account is 2.

    > Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

CreateDeviceTunnel.title: Create a Device Secure Tunnel
CreateDeviceTunnel.summary: Create a secure tunnel for a specified device.
CreateDeviceTunnel.description:
## How-To

After you successfully invoke this API to create a secure tunnel, the status of the secure tunnel is **open** by default.
- 24 hours after creation, the secure tunnel status is automatically updated to **closed**.
- 30 days after creation, the secure tunnel is automatically deleted by the system.

## Limits

- A single device can have up to 10 secure tunnels.
- A single instance can contain up to 1,000 secure tunnels.

## QPS Limit

The maximum queries per second (QPS) for this API per Alibaba Cloud account is 5.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

CreateDownloadDataJob.title: CreateDownloadDataJob
CreateDownloadDataJob.summary: Invoke the API to create a data download job.
CreateDownloadDataJob.description:
## How-To

- This job is equivalent to a data download job created in the console. You can view the log of this download job and download the file on the export management page of the corresponding data table.

- Creating a download job through this API triggers an [AMQP message push](~~143601~~). Use `dop_aliyun_group_name` as the `consumerGroupId`. The message content includes the execution status of this download job. You can use this status together with the [GetDownloadFile](~~445783~~) API to obtain the file download URL or view abnormal information about the download job.

## Limits

- Only one download job can be created at a time under the same data instance. You must wait until the previous job finishes before creating a new one. Otherwise, an exception indicating that the limit on the number of download jobs has been exceeded is returned.

- The maximum time range for data in a single download is 3 days.

- You can create up to 3 download jobs per day. Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

schema.description: The ID of the Internet of Things (IoT) service instance. This parameter is not required for the public instance but required for Enterprise Edition instances.

The ID of the driver. To obtain the driver ID, perform the following steps: Log on to the [Link IoT Edge console](https://iot.console.aliyun.com/le/instance/list). On the **Drivers** page, move the pointer over the name of the driver for which you want to create a driver version and obtain the driver ID.

You can also call the [QueryEdgeDriver](~~155776~~) operation to query the driver ID.

The version number of the driver. The version number must be unique for the driver. The version number can be up to 64 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, underscores (\_), hyphens (-), and periods (.).

The earliest version of Link IoT Edge that is supported by the driver. The driver can run on gateways of only this version and later. For example, if you set this parameter to 2.4.0, the driver can run on gateways of only version 2.4.0 and later.
The description of the driver. The description can be a maximum of 256 bytes in length.

The source of the driver code. Set this parameter to a JSON string in the following format:

`{"ossAddress":"http://***/driver_code.zip"}`

In the JSON string, `ossAddress` specifies the URL of the driver code stored in Object Storage Service (OSS). If you want to upload the driver code and obtain the URL of the driver code stored in OSS by using API operations, call the [CreateOssPreSignedAddress](~~155858~~) operation first.

The configuration of the driver. Set this parameter to a JSON string in the following format:

`{"format":"JSON","content":"{}"}`

The JSON string contains the following parameters:

*   format: the format of the driver configuration. Valid values: KV (key-value pair), JSON (JSON string), and FILE (configuration file).

*   content: the content of the driver configuration. If you set the format parameter to KV or JSON, set this parameter to the configuration content of the driver. If you set the format parameter to FILE, set this parameter to the URL of the driver configuration file stored in OSS.

> To obtain the URL of the driver configuration file stored in OSS, call the [CreateOssPreSignedAddress](~~155858~~) operation.

The configuration of the container where the driver runs. Set this parameter to a JSON string. For more information about parameters in the JSON string, see the following parameter description of **ContainerConfig**.

The rule for verifying configurations. Set this parameter to a JSON string in the following format:

`{"deviceConfig":{"required":false},"driverConfig":{"required":false}`

The JSON string contains the following parameters:

*   driverConfig: the rule for verifying the configuration of the driver when the driver is to be deployed in an edge instance.
*   deviceConfig: the rule for verifying the configurations of devices that use the driver when the driver is to be deployed in an edge instance.

`required`: A value of true indicates that the corresponding parameter is required. A value of false indicates that the corresponding parameter is optional.

**Parameter description of ContainerConfig**| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| privileged | Integer | No | Specifies whether to enable the privilege mode for the container. Valid values:

0: disables the mode.

1: enables the mode. |
| hostNetworkMode | Integer | No | Specifies whether to enable the host mode for the container. Valid values:

0: disables the mode.

1: enables the mode. |
| portMappings | List | No | The mapping of network ports. This parameter is not required if the hostNetworkMode parameter is set to 1. You can specify a maximum of 10 mapping records in this parameter. For more information about specific parameters, see the following parameter description of portMappings. |
| devMappings | List | No | The mapping of devices. This parameter is not required if the privileged parameter is set to 1. You can specify a maximum of 10 mapping records in this parameter. For more information about specific parameters, see the following parameter description of devMappings. |
| volumeMappings | List | No | The mapping of volumes. You can specify a maximum of 10 mapping records in this parameter. For more information about specific parameters, see the following parameter description of volumeMappings. |
**Parameter description of portMappings**| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| hostPort | Integer | Yes | The port number of the host where the container resides. Valid values: 1 to 65535. |
| containerPort | Integer | Yes | The port number of the container. Valid values: 1 to 65535. |
| protocol | Integer | Yes | The type of the protocol that is used for communication between the mapping ports. Valid values: tcp and udp. |
**Parameter description of devMappings**| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| hostPath | String | Yes | The name of the device that the driver needs to access. The name must be 1 to 128 characters in length and start with **/dev/**. |
| permission | String | Yes | The permissions that the driver has for the device. Valid values:

ro: The driver has only the read permissions for the device.

rw: The driver has both the read and write permissions for the device. |
| comment | String | No | The remarks for the mapping. The remarks must be 1 to 128 characters in length. |
**Parameter description of volumeMappings**| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| hostPath | String | Yes | The host path of the volume that the driver needs to access. The path must be 1 to 128 characters in length and cannot contain spaces. |
| containerPath | String | Yes | The path for accessing the volume in the container. The path must be an absolute path that starts with a forward slash (/). The path must be 2 to 128 characters in length and cannot contain spaces. Do not set this parameter to the root directory. |
| permission | String | Yes | The permissions that the driver has for the volume. Valid values:

ro: The driver has only the read permissions for the volume.

rw: The driver has both the read and write permissions for the volume. |

**TargetConfig Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |TargetType|String|The configuration type of the target devices. Valid values:
**DEVICE_LIST**: indicates a list of devices.

**PRODUCT_KEY**: indicates the **ProductKey** of the product to which the devices belong.| |TargetDevices|List|The target devices for the job. This parameter is required only when **TargetType** is set to **DEVICE_LIST**.
You can specify up to 200 devices in this parameter.
For more information, see "TargetDevice Definition" below.| |TargetGroup|String|The identifier (GroupID) of the device group to which the target devices belong. This parameter is required only when **TargetType** is set to **GROUP_ID**.
Dynamic device group IDs are not supported.
The device group can contain up to 100,000 devices.| |TargetProduct|String|The **ProductKey** of the product to which the target devices belong. This parameter is required only when **TargetType** is set to **PRODUCT_KEY**.
The product can contain up to 100,000 devices.| **TargetDevice Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |IotId|String|The device ID of the target device.| |ProductKey|String|The **ProductKey** of the product to which the target device belongs.
If you specify this parameter, you must also specify **DeviceName**.| |DeviceName|String|The name of the target device.
If you specify this parameter, you must also specify **ProductKey**.| Example 1 ``` { "TargetDevices": [ { "IotId":"OPx***00101", "ProductKey":"a1A***n", "DeviceName":"devicenew" } ], "TargetType":"DEVICE_LIST" } ``` Example 2 ``` { "targetGroup":"rY2***01", "targetType":"GROUP_ID" } ``` Example 3 ``` { "targetType":"PRODUCT_KEY", "targetProduct":"a1j***3d" } ``` **RolloutConfig Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |maximumPerMinute|Integer|The maximum number of jobs pushed per minute under the task. Default value: 1000. Valid values: 50 to 1000.| |messageQoS|String|The message type for sending messages. This parameter applies only to custom jobs and batch Pub message push jobs. Valid values:
**QoS0**: indicates that the message is sent at most once.
**QoS1**: indicates that the message is sent at least once. If a QoS1 message does not receive a PUBACK response, it will be resent to the device upon reconnection.| Example ``` { "maximumPerMinute": 1000, "messageQoS":"QoS1" } ``` **TimeoutConfig Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |inProgressTimeoutInMinutes|Integer|The timeout period (in minutes) for job execution under the task.
This parameter applies only to custom jobs.
The timeout period starts when the task begins execution (status changes to **IN_PROGRESS**). If the job is not completed within this period, its status is automatically set to TIMED_OUT.
Valid values:
For **INVOKE_SERVICE** tasks: maximum value is 5, minimum value is 1, default value is 1.
For **SET_PROPERTY** tasks: maximum value is 5, minimum value is 1, default value is 1.
For **CUSTOM_JOB** tasks: maximum value is 3600, minimum value is 1, default value is 60.| Example ``` { "inProgressTimeoutInMinutes": 60 } ``` **JobDocument Definition** Jobs of type **INVOKE_SERVICE** are used to invoke device services in batches, similar to the [InvokeThingsService](~~96242~~) API. |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |serviceIdentifier|String|The identifier of the service.
You can view this identifier in the IoT Platform console. Navigate to **Device Management > Products**, find the product to which the device belongs, and check the **Feature Definition** section on the product details page.| |params|Object|The input parameters for invoking the service. For more information, see "params Definition" below.| **params Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |key|String|The identifier of the input parameter, which you defined when creating the service.
In the IoT Platform console, on the Feature Definition page of the product to which the device belongs, you can view the input parameters either from the Thing Specification Language model or by clicking the Edit button next to the service.| |value|String|The parameter value. The value must fall within the range you defined for the input parameter.| Example ``` { "serviceIdentifier": "test_service", "params": { "key1": "value1", "key2": "value2" } } ``` Jobs of type **SET_PROPERTY** are used to set device property values in batches, similar to the [SetDevicesProperty](~~96243~~) API. |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |params|Object|The properties to be set, in key:value format. For more information, see "params Definition" below.| **params Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |key|String|The identifier of the property to be set. You can view this identifier in the IoT Platform console under the Feature Definition section of the product to which the device belongs.
The property must be read-write. If you specify a read-only property, the setting will fail.| |value|String|The property value. The value must match the data type and range you defined for the property.| ``` { "params": { "key1": "value1", "key2": "value2" } } ``` **CUSTOM_JOB** represents a custom job. |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |key|String|Custom property.| |value|String|Custom property value.| ``` { "key":"value" } ``` **JobFile Definition** |Name|Type|Description| |------|------|------| |fileKey|String|The **Key** of the file generated by calling the **GenerateFileUploadURL** API.
You must upload the file before creating the job. For details, see the "How-To" section of [GenerateFileUploadURL](~~198575~~).
The system validates whether the file has been uploaded when the job is created.| |signMethod|String|The signature method. Valid values: MD5 and SHA256.| |sign|String|The signature of the file uploaded via URL, generated using the specified signature method.| Example ``` { "fileKey":"5cc34***/tazJff***", "signMethod":"", "sign":"" } ``` When calling this API, in addition to the specific request parameters described in this topic, you must also pass common request parameters. schema.description:
The ID of the update package.

An update package ID is returned when you call the [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) operation to create the update package.

You can also call the [ListOTAFirmware](~~147450~~) operation to obtain the ID.

The **ProductKey** of the product to which the update package belongs.

A **ProductKey** is the unique identifier of a product in IoT Platform. You can view the information about all products within the current Alibaba Cloud account in the IoT Platform console or by calling the [QueryProductList](~~69271~~) operation.

The automatic retry interval if a device fails to be updated. Unit: minutes. Valid values:

*   **0**: An automatic retry is immediately performed.
*   **10**: An automatic retry is performed after 10 minutes.
*   **30**: An automatic retry is performed after 30 minutes.
*   **60**: An automatic retry is performed after 60 minutes (1 hour).
*   **1440**: An automatic retry is performed after 1,440 minutes (24 hours).

> The value of the **RetryInterval** parameter must be less than the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter. Examples:
>*   If the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter is set to 60, the maximum value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is 30.
>*   If the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter is set to 1440, the maximum value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is 60.

If the value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is set to 1440, we recommend that you do not specify the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter. If an update times out, no retry is performed.

If you do not specify this parameter, no retry is performed.

The number of automatic retries.

If you specify the **RetryInterval** parameter, you must specify this parameter.

Valid values:

*   **1**: retries once.
*   **2**: retries twice.
*   **5**: retries five times.

The timeout period of the update. If the device is not updated within the specified period, a timeout error occurs. Unit: minutes. Valid values: 1 to 1440.

> *   The timeout period starts from the time when the specified device submits the update progress for the first time. During the update, the update package may be repeatedly pushed to the specified device because the device goes online and offline multiple times. The start time of the update period remains unchanged.
>*   If an update fails due to timeout, no retry is triggered.

If you do not specify this parameter, timeout errors do not occur.

The maximum number of devices to which the download URL of the update package is pushed per minute. Valid values: 10 to 10000.

Default value: 10000.

Specifies whether to overwrite the previous update task. Default value: 1. Valid values:

*   **1**: The previous update task is not overwritten. If a device already has an update task, the previous update task is implemented.
*   **2**: The previous update task is overwritten. Only the current update task is implemented. In this case, you cannot set **MultiModuleMode** to **true**.

>  The update task that is in progress is not overwritten.

The mode of dynamic update. Default value: 1. Valid values:

*   **1**: constantly updates the devices that meet the conditions.
*   **2**: updates only the devices that subsequently submit the latest firmware versions.

Specifies whether to automatically push update tasks from IoT Platform to devices. Default value: true. Valid values:

*   **true**: After an update batch is created, IoT Platform automatically pushes update tasks to the specified online devices.

    In this case, a device can still initiate a request to obtain the information about the over-the-air (OTA) update task from IoT Platform.

*   **false**: A device must initiate a request to obtain the information about the OTA update task from IoT Platform.

Specifies whether to control the update by using a mobile app. You must develop the mobile app as needed. Default value: false. Valid values:

*   **false**: A device obtains the information about the OTA update task based on the **NeedPush** parameter.
*   **true**: To perform an OTA update on a device, you must confirm the update by using your mobile app. Then, the device can obtain the information about the OTA update task based on the **NeedPush** parameter.

The ID of the group.

*   If you specify this parameter, you must also specify the **GroupType** parameter. In this case, do not specify the **SrcVersion.N** parameter.
*   If you do not specify this parameter, you do not need to specify the **GroupType** parameter. In this case, you must specify the **SrcVersion.N** parameter.

You can call the [QueryDeviceGroupList](~~93356~~) operation to query the **GroupId** parameter.

The type of the group. Valid value: **LINK_PLATFORM_DYNAMIC**.

*   If you specify this parameter, you must also specify the **GroupId** parameter. In this case, do not specify the **SrcVersion.N** parameter.
*   If you do not specify this parameter, you do not need to specify the **GroupId** parameter. In this case, you must specify the **SrcVersion.N** parameter.

The download protocol of the update package. Valid values: **HTTPS** and **MQTT**. Default value: HTTPS. After the device receives the update package information pushed by IoT Platform, this protocol is used to download the update package.

> If you need to download the update package over MQTT, take note of the following items:
>*   Your service must be deployed in the China (Shanghai) region.
>*   The OTA update package can contain only one file, and the size of the file cannot exceed 16 MB.
>*   You must use the latest version of Link SDK for C to develop the device features to perform OTA updates and download files over MQTT. For more information, see [Sample code](~~330985~~).

Specifies whether the device supports simultaneous updates of multiple modules. Default value: false. Valid values:

*   **false**

*   **true**: In this case, do not set **OverwriteMode** to **2**.********

    The update tasks for the same module are overwritten. The update tasks that are in progress are not overwritten. The update tasks of the modules do not affect each other.

>*   Only Enterprise Edition instances and new public instances are supported.
>*   You must use Link SDK for C 4.x to develop the device.
>*   If you initiate a group-based dynamic update batch, the settings of **MultiModuleMode** and **OverwriteMode** must be the same as those in the existing dynamic update batch of the group.

For more information, see [Overview](~~58328~~).

The list of firmware versions to be updated.

*   If you specify this parameter, do not specify the **GroupId** and **GroupType** parameters.
*   If you do not specify this parameter, you must specify the **GroupId** and **GroupType** parameters.

> If you use differential update packages to perform dynamic update tasks on dynamic groups, you do not need to specify this parameter.
>*   If you use differential update packages to perform dynamic update tasks based on versions, the value of this parameter must be the same as the value of **SrcVersion**.
>*   You can call the [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) operation and view the **FirmwareVersion** parameter in the response.
>*   The version numbers must be unique in the list.
>*   You can specify a maximum of 10 version numbers.

A list of version numbers to be upgraded.

- If you specify this parameter, you cannot specify **GroupId** or **GroupType**.
- If you do not specify this parameter, you must specify both **GroupId** and **GroupType**.

> - When initiating a dynamic upgrade job for a delta update package based on specific versions, the value of this parameter must match the source version (**SrcVersion**) of the delta update package.
- When initiating a dynamic upgrade job for a delta update package based on a dynamic group, you do not need to specify this parameter.
- You can call [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) to view the OTA module version (**FirmwareVersion**) of a device.
- The list must not contain duplicate version numbers.
- You can specify up to 10 version numbers.

CreateOTADynamicUpgradeJob.title: CreateOTADynamicUpgradeJob
CreateOTADynamicUpgradeJob.summary: Invoke this API to create a dynamic over-the-air update job.
CreateOTADynamicUpgradeJob.description:
## How-To

- If you did not specify that firmware verification is not required when you called [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) to create an upgrade package, you must ensure that the upgrade package has been successfully verified before calling this API to create a batch upgrade job. For information about how to create a verification job for an upgrade package, see [CreateOTAVerifyJob](~~147480~~).
- A device can be included in only one upgrade job at a time in either the pending or upgrading status. If you initiate a new upgrade job for a device that is already in the pending or upgrading status, the new job immediately fails.
- Only one dynamic upgrade job can be in the executing status for the same upgrade package.
- If a device is included in dynamic upgrade policies of different upgrade packages, the device executes the most recently initiated dynamic upgrade.
- After you create a dynamic upgrade job, the system automatically creates a corresponding dynamic upgrade policy. You can call [CancelOTAStrategyByJob](~~147905~~) to cancel the dynamic upgrade policy.
- Currently, only Enterprise instances and new public instances in the China (Shanghai) region support creating dynamic upgrade jobs for dynamic groups.<props="china"><ph>For more information about instances, see [Instance Management](~~147356~~).</ph></props>
- Currently, only the China (Shanghai), China (Beijing), and China (Shenzhen) regions support downloading upgrade packages over the MQTT protocol.

## queries per second (QPS) limit

The maximum queries per second (QPS) for a single Alibaba Cloud account when calling this API is 20.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

schema.description:
The ID of the instance. You can view the ID of the instance on the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console.

>*   If your instance has an ID, you must specify the ID for this parameter. Otherwise, the call fails.
>*   If no **Overview** page or **ID** is generated for your instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

The name of the OTA update package. The name must be unique within an Alibaba Cloud account. The name cannot be modified after the OTA update package is created. The name must be 1 to 40 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, hyphens (-), underscores (\_), and parentheses (). The name must start with a letter or a digit.
The version number of the OTA update package. The value can contain letters, digits, periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (\_). The version number must be 1 to 64 characters in length.

The URL of the OTA update package. This parameter specifies the storage location of the OTA update package in OSS. You can call the [GenerateOTAUploadURL](~~147310~~) operation to generate a URL for the OTA update package.

>If you add only one file to the OTA update package, you must configure this parameter.

The signature of the OTA update package. The value is calculated by using the specified **signature algorithm** to sign the OTA update package.

> If you add only one file to the OTA update package, you can configure this parameter. If you do not configure this parameter, the MD5 value of the OTA update package in OSS is used as the package signature.

The signature algorithm of the OTA update package. Set the value to **MD5**. The value indicates an MD5 signature.

Default value: **MD5**.

The size of the OTA update package. Unit: bytes.

> If you add only one file to the OTA update package, you can configure this parameter. If you do not configure this parameter, the size of the OTA update package in OSS is used.
The **ProductKey** of the product to which the OTA update package belongs.
The description of the OTA update package. The description must be 1 to 100 characters in length.

The type of the OTA update package. Valid values:

*   **0**: The uploaded file contains a full update package. IoT Platform pushes the full update package to a device for update.
*   **1**: The uploaded file contains only the differences between the latest update package and the previous update package. IoT Platform pushes only the differences to a device for update.

Default value: **0**.

The version number of the OTA module of the device to be updated.

You can call the [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) operation and view the **FirmwareVersion** parameter in the response.

> *   If you set the **Type** parameter to **1**, you must configure this parameter, and the value cannot be the same as the update package version that is specified by the **DestVersion** parameter.
>*   If you set the **Type** parameter to **0**, this parameter is optional.

The name of the OTA module. OTA modules are the updatable units of devices that belong to the same product.

> *   If you do not configure this parameter, the default OTA module is used. The default value indicates that the complete device firmware is updated.
>*   You can call the [CreateOTAModule](~~186066~~) operation to create a custom OTA module. You can call the [ListOTAModuleByProduct](~~186532~~) operation to query the existing OTA modules of a product.

Specifies whether to verify the OTA update package before you create a batch update task.

*   **true** The system verifies the OTA update package before you create a batch update task. This is the default value.
*   **false**: The system does not verify the OTA update package before you create a batch update task.

The custom information that you want to send to a device. The format of the custom information has no limits. However, the information cannot exceed 4,096 characters in length.

After you add the OTA update package and create an update task, IoT Platform sends the custom information to the specified device when IoT Platform pushes an update notification.

## How-To  
Before invoking this API to create an upgrade package, you have already invoked [GenerateOTAUploadURL](~~147310~~) to generate upload information for the upgrade package and used the OSS [PostObject](~~31988~~) API to upload the upgrade package file.

> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

CreateOTAModule.title: CreateOTAModule
CreateOTAModule.summary: Creates an over-the-air (OTA) module for a product.
CreateOTAModule.description:
## Limits

OTA modules are the updatable units of the devices that belong to the same product. The default module indicates the entire firmware of a device. You can call this operation to create a custom OTA module.

*   You can create a maximum of 10 custom OTA modules for each product.

*   After an OTA module is created, you cannot modify its name. You can call the [UpdateOTAModule](~~186061~~) operation to modify the module alias and description.

*   Each Alibaba Cloud account can run a maximum of 10 queries per second (QPS).

> RAM users of an Alibaba Cloud account share the quota of the account.
CreateOTAModule.requestParamsDescription: In addition to the preceding operation-specific request parameters, you must specify common request parameters when you call this operation. For more information, see [Common request parameters](~~30561~~).

schema.description:
The ID of the instance. You can view the ID of an instance on the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console.

>*   If your instance has an ID, you must specify the ID for this parameter. If you do not specify the instance ID, the call fails.****
>*   If no **Overview** page or **ID** is generated for your instance, you do not need to configure this parameter.

For more information, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

The ID of the update package.

An update package ID is returned when you call the [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) operation to create the update package.

You can also call the [ListOTAFirmware](~~147450~~) operation to obtain the ID.

The **ProductKey** of the product to which the update package belongs.

A **ProductKey** is the unique identifier of a product in IoT Platform. You can view the information about all products within the current Alibaba Cloud account in the IoT Platform console or by calling the [QueryProductList](~~69271~~) operation.

The scope of the update batch. Valid values:

*   **ALL**: updates all devices.
*   **SPECIFIC**: updates specified devices.
*   **GRAY**: performs a phased update.
*   **GROUP**: updates specified groups.

The time to start the over-the-air (OTA) update.

The scheduled time ranges from 5 minutes to 7 days later than the current time. The value must be a 13-digit timestamp.

If you do not specify this parameter, the update immediately starts.

The automatic retry interval if a device fails to be updated. Unit: minutes. Valid values:

*   **0**: An automatic retry is immediately performed.
*   **10**: An automatic retry is performed after 10 minutes.
*   **30**: An automatic retry is performed after 30 minutes.
*   **60**: An automatic retry is performed after 60 minutes (1 hour).
*   **1440**: An automatic retry is performed after 1,440 minutes (24 hours).

> The value of the **RetryInterval** parameter must be less than the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter. Examples:
>*   If the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter is set to 60, the maximum value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is 30.
>*   If the value of the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter is set to 1440, the maximum value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is 60.

If the value of the **RetryInterval** parameter is set to 1440, we recommend that you do not specify the **TimeoutInMinutes** parameter. If an update times out, no retry is performed.

If you do not specify this parameter, no retry is performed.

The number of automatic retries.

If you specify the **RetryInterval** parameter, you must specify this parameter.

Valid values:

*   **1**: retries once.
*   **2**: retries twice.
*   **5**: retries five times.

The timeout period of the update. If the device is not updated within the specified period, a timeout error occurs. Unit: minutes. Valid values: 1 to 1440.

> *   The timeout period starts from the time when the specified device submits the update progress for the first time. During the update, the update package may be repeatedly pushed to the specified device because the device goes online and offline multiple times. The start time of the update period remains unchanged.
>*   If an update fails due to timeout, no retry is triggered.

If you do not specify this parameter, timeout errors do not occur.

The maximum number of devices to which the download URL of the update package is pushed per minute. Valid values: 10 to 10000.

Default value: 10000.

The ratio of the phased update. The value is a percentage in the string format. It can be up to three decimal places. The calculated number of devices is rounded down to the nearest integer. You must specify at least one device for a phased update.

For example, if you set the phased update ratio to 33.33 for 100 devices, the number of devices to be updated is 33.

You must specify this parameter if you set the TargetSelection parameter to `GRAY`.

The time to end the update.

The end time must be 1 hour to 30 days later than the start time that is specified by the **ScheduleTime** parameter. The value must be a 13-digit timestamp.

If you do not specify this parameter, the update is not forcibly ended.

Specifies whether to overwrite the previous update task. Default value: 1. Valid values:

*   **1**: The previous update task is not overwritten. If a device already has an update task, the previous update task is implemented.
*   **2**: The previous update task is overwritten. Only the current update task is implemented. In this case, you cannot set **MultiModuleMode** to **true**.

>  The update task that is in progress is not overwritten.

The URL of the device list file that is used to perform a specific update.

> *   If you set the TargetSelection parameter to `SPECIFIC`, you must specify this parameter or the **TargetDeviceName.N** parameter. You cannot specify the two parameters at the same time.
>*   You can call the [GenerateDeviceNameListURL](~~186062~~) operation to generate a file URL. Then, you can perform the operations as prompted to upload the device list file.
>*   During a full update, the devices that have been updated are skipped.
>*   During a delta update, the devices that have been updated and the devices whose initial version numbers are different from the update package are skipped.

Specifies whether to automatically push update tasks from IoT Platform to devices. Default value: true. Valid values:

*   **true**: After an update batch is created, IoT Platform automatically pushes update tasks to the specified online devices.

    In this case, a device can still initiate a request to obtain the information about the over-the-air (OTA) update task from IoT Platform.

*   **false**: A device must initiate a request to obtain the information about the OTA update task from IoT Platform.

Specifies whether to control the update by using a mobile app. You must develop the mobile app as needed. Default false: true. Valid values:

*   **false**: A device obtains the information about the OTA update task based on the **NeedPush** parameter.
*   **true**: To perform an OTA update on a device, you must confirm the update by using your mobile app. Then, the device can obtain the information about the OTA update task based on the **NeedPush** parameter.

The ID of the group.

If you set the TargetSelection parameter to `GROUP`, you must specify this parameter and the **GroupType** parameter.

You can call the [QueryDeviceGroupList](~~93356~~) operation to query the **GroupId** parameter.

The type of the group. Valid value: **LINK_PLATFORM**.

If you set the TargetSelection parameter to `GROUP`, you must specify this parameter and the **GroupId** parameter.

The download protocol of the update package. Valid values: **HTTPS** and **MQTT**. Default value: HTTPS. After the device receives the update package information pushed by IoT Platform, this protocol is used to download the update package.

>If you need to download the update package over MQTT, take note of the following items:
>*   Your service must be deployed in the China (Shanghai), China (Beijing), or China (Shenzhen) region.
>*   The OTA update package can contain only one file, and the size of the file cannot exceed 16 MB.
>*   You must use the latest version of Link SDK for C to develop the device features to perform OTA updates and download files over MQTT. For more information, see [Sample code](~~330985~~).

Specifies whether the device supports simultaneous updates of multiple modules. Default value: false. Valid values:

*   **false**

*   **true**: In this case, do not set **OverwriteMode** to **2**.********

    The update tasks for the same module are overwritten. The update tasks that are in progress are not overwritten. The update tasks of the modules do not affect each other.

>*   Only Enterprise Edition instances and new public instances are supported.
>*   You must use Link SDK for C 4.x to develop the device.

For more information, see [Overview](~~58328~~).

A list of version numbers to be upgraded.

>- You can provide this parameter when initiating a full upgrade (`TargetSelection=ALL`) or a grayscale upgrade (`TargetSelection=GRAY`).
- When using a delta update package to initiate a full or grayscale upgrade, the value of this parameter must be the source version number (**SrcVersion**) of the delta update package.
- You cannot provide this parameter when initiating a targeted upgrade (`TargetSelection=SPECIFIC`) or a group upgrade (`TargetSelection=GROUP`).
- You can call [QueryDeviceDetail](~~69594~~) to check the OTA module version number (**FirmwareVersion**) of a device.
- The list must not contain duplicate version numbers.
- You can specify up to 10 version numbers.

>*   This parameter is unavailable if you set the TargetSelection parameter to `SPECIFIC` or `GROUP`.

CreateOTAStaticUpgradeJob.title: CreateOTAStaticUpgradeJob
CreateOTAStaticUpgradeJob.summary: Invoke this API to create a static over-the-air update job.
CreateOTAStaticUpgradeJob.description:
## How-To

- If you do not specify "The firmware package can bypass verification" when calling the [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) API to create an upgrade package, you must ensure that the upgrade package has passed verification before calling this API to create a batch upgrade job. For information about how to create a verification job for an upgrade package, see [CreateOTAVerifyJob](~~147480~~).
- In a single API call for targeted upgrades:
  - If you directly specify device names, you can initiate an upgrade job for up to 200 devices.
  - If you use a file containing the list of devices to be upgraded, you can initiate an upgrade job for up to 10,000 devices. Before doing so, you must call [GenerateDeviceNameListURL](~~186062~~) to generate a file URL and upload the device list file as instructed.
- When initiating an upgrade job for multiple devices, if a device is already running the target version, that device is filtered out and the upgrade job continues for the remaining devices.
- A single device can be included in only one upgrade job at a time in either the pending or upgrading state. If you initiate a new upgrade job for a device that is already in the pending or upgrading state, the new job fails immediately.
- You can initiate multiple static upgrade jobs simultaneously for the same upgrade package.
- In the Japan (Tokyo) and US (Virginia) regions, creating static group-based upgrade jobs is not supported. That is, the **TargetSelection** parameter does not support the value **GROUP**.
- Currently, downloading upgrade packages using the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol is supported only in the China (Shanghai), China (Beijing), and China (Shenzhen) regions.

## Queries per second (QPS) limit

A single Alibaba Cloud account can send a maximum of 20 requests per second (QPS) to call this API.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

CreateOTAVerifyJob.title: CreateOTAVerifyJob
CreateOTAVerifyJob.summary: Invoke this API to create an over-the-air (OTA) update package verification job.
CreateOTAVerifyJob.description:
## How-To  

- You must verify the OTA update package before pushing it to devices for batch upgrades. Only verified OTA update packages can be used for batch device upgrades. You can call [QueryOTAFirmware](~~147461~~) to view the verification status of an OTA update package.  
- You cannot initiate a new verification job for an OTA update package that is currently being verified or has already been successfully verified.  
- You can specify up to 10 devices for OTA update package verification.  

## QPS Limit  
The maximum queries per second (QPS) for a single Alibaba Cloud account calling this API is 10.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

schema.description:

For more information about the instance, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

The name of the product.

The name must be 4 to 30 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, and underscores (\_).


**Important** Each product name must be unique within the current instance.

The node type of the product. Valid values:

*   **0**: device. Sub-devices cannot be attached to a device. A device can be directly connected to IoT Platform or connected to IoT Platform as a sub-device of a gateway. If you use the device as a sub-device, you must also configure the **ProtocolType** parameter.
*   **1**: gateway. Sub-devices can be attached to a gateway. A gateway can manage sub-devices, maintain topological relationships with sub-devices, and synchronize topological relationships to IoT Platform.

The data format.

If the **AliyunCommodityCode** parameter is set to **iothub_senior**, you must configure this parameter.

Valid values:

*   **0**: custom data format.
*   **1**: Alink JSON format.
The description of the product. The description can be up to 100 characters in length.

The edition of the product.

*   If you do not configure this parameter, a product of the Basic Edition is automatically created. You cannot use a TSL model to define the product.
*   If you want to configure this parameter, set the value to **iothub_senior**. A product that supports TSL models is created. You must also configure the **DataFormat** parameter.
You do not need to configure this parameter.

The protocol used by the devices of the product to connect to the gateway.

If the **AliyunCommodityCode** parameter is set to **iothub_senior** and a gateway is required to connect the devices of the product to IoT Platform, you must configure this parameter.

Valid values:

*   **modbus**: Modbus.
*   **opc-ua**: Open Platform Communication Unified Architecture (OPC UA).
*   **customize**: custom protocol.
*   **ble**: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE).
*   **zigbee**: ZigBee.

The network connection method.

If the **AliyunCommodityCode** parameter is set to **iothub_senior** and the devices of the product are directly connected devices or gateways, you must configure this parameter.

Valid values:

*   **WIFI**: Wi-Fi.
*   **CELLULAR**: cellular network.
*   **ETHERNET**: Ethernet.
*   **OTHER**: other networks.

Default value: WIFI.
You do not need to configure this parameter.

The ID of the resource group to which the product belongs. If you specify a value for this parameter, the product is added to the resource group.

You can log on to the [Resource Management console](https://resourcemanager.console.aliyun.com/resource-groups) to view the ID of the resource group.


**Important**

You can specify a value for this parameter only if you have activated Resource Management.

The verification method that is used to connect the devices of the product to IoT Platform.

You do not need to configure this parameter. **secret**: uses DeviceSecrets to verify the devices. Default value: secret. For more information, see [MQTT connections over TCP](~~73742~~).

The identifier of the product category. If you configure this parameter, a TSL model of the product category is used. Otherwise, no TSL model is used.

You can call the [ListThingTemplates](~~150316~~) operation to query the details of product categories that are predefined by IoT Platform and obtain category keys.

Specifies whether to publish the TSL model after the product is created.

*   **true**: publishes the TSL model after the product is created.
*   **false**: does not publish the TSL model after the product is created.

Default value: **true**.

The level of data verification. If you do not configure this parameter, the default value is used. Valid values:

*   **1**: weak verification. Default value: 1. IoT Platform verifies only the identifier and dataType fields of the data. All data is forwarded.

    In the IoT Platform console, the data is displayed on the **TSL Data** tab of the **Device Details** page. The data that fails to be verified is not displayed.

    You can view the data that failed to be verified in the **checkFailedData** parameter of the forwarded data. For more information, see [Data formats](~~73736~~).

*   **2**: no verification. IoT Platform does not verify the data. All data is forwarded.

    In the IoT Platform console, the data is not displayed on the **TSL Data** tab of the **Device Details** page.

## How-To

- The **Endpoint** for accessing Alibaba Cloud services supports only China (Shanghai), which is `iot.cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com`.

- You cannot use this API to create cross-account distribution jobs.

- A product distribution job does not synchronize devices under the product.

- After a product is distributed, you cannot modify the Thing Specification Language model or related scripts of the product.

- The total number of product distribution and device distribution jobs under a single Alibaba Cloud account cannot exceed 10. For information about how to create a device distribution job, see [CreateDeviceDistributeJob](~~199390~~).

- The maximum queries per second (QPS) for invoking this API under a single Alibaba Cloud account is 2.

schema.description:
The topic to which this rule is applied. Format: `${deviceName}/topicShortName`. `${deviceName}` specifies the name of the device, and `topicShortName` specifies the custom name of the topic.

*   Basic communication topics or Thing Specification Language (TSL)-based communication topics. Format: `${deviceName}/topicShortName`. You can replace `${deviceName}` with the `+` wildcard character. The wildcard character indicates that the topic applies to all devices under the product. Valid values of `topicShortName`:

    *   `/thing/event/property/post`: submits the property data of a device.

    *   `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: submits the event data of a device. `${tsl.event.identifier}` specifies the identifier of an event in the TSL model.

    *   `/thing/lifecycle`: submits device lifecycle changes.

    *   `/thing/downlink/reply/message`: sends a response to a request from IoT Platform.

    *   `/thing/list/found`: submits the data when a gateway detects a new sub-device.

    *   `/thing/topo/lifecycle`: submits device topology changes.

    *   `/thing/event/property/history/post`: submits the historical property data of a device.

    *   `/thing/event/${tsl.event.identifier}/post`: submits the historical event data of a device. `${tsl.event.identifier}` specifies the identifier of an event in the TSL model.

    *   `/ota/upgrade`: submits the OTA update status.

    *   `/ota/version/post`: submits OTA module versions.

    *   `/thing/deviceinfo/update`: submits device tag changes.

    *   `/edge/driver/${driver_id}/point_post`: submits pass-through data from Link IoT Edge. `${driver_id}` specifies the ID of the driver that a device uses to access Link IoT Edge.

        The `${packageId}/${jobId}/ota/job/status` topic submits the status of OTA update batches. This topic is a basic communication topic. `${packageId}` specifies the ID of the update package. `${jobId}` specifies the ID of the update batch.

*   Custom topics. Example: `${deviceName}/user/get`.

    You can call the [QueryProductTopic](~~69647~~) operation to view all custom topics of the product.

    When you specify a custom topic, you can use the `+` and `#` wildcard characters.

    *   You can replace `${deviceName}` with the `+` wildcard character. The wildcard character specifies that the topic applies to all devices in the product.

    *   You can add `/user/#` after ${deviceName}. The `#` wildcard character can match all field values at the levels that follow `/user`.

        For more information about how to use wildcard characters, see [Custom topics with one or more wildcard characters](~~85539~~).

*   Topics that are used to submit device status changes. The topic name is in the `${deviceName}` format.

    You can use the `+` wildcard character. In this case, the status changes of all devices under the product are submitted.

The condition that is used to trigger the rule. For more information about the rule, see [SQL statements](~~30554~~).

If you do not specify this parameter, the rule is assigned to the default resource group.

The ID of the rule for which you want to create an action. You can log on to the IoT Platform console, and choose **Rules** > **Data Forwarding** to view the rule ID. You can also call the [ListRule](~~69486~~) operation and view the rule ID in the response.

The type of the rule action. Valid values:

*   **REPUBLISH**: forwards topic data that is processed by the rules engine to another IoT Platform topic.
*   **AMQP**: forwards data to an AMQP consumer group.
*   **MNS**: forwards data that is processed by the rules engine to Message Service (MNS).
*   **FC**: forwards topic data that is processed by the rules engine to Function Compute for event computing.
*   **OTS**: forwards data that is processed by the rules engine to OTS for NoSQL data storage.

>  If you set the **DataType** parameter to **BINARY**, rules are created in the binary format. These rules cannot be used to forward data to Tablestore.

The configurations of the rule action. You must specify a JSON string. The configurations vary based on the types of rule actions. For more information about required syntax and examples, see the following tables.

Specifies whether the rule action forwards error operation data. Error operation data is generated when the rules engine failed to forward data from the IoT Platform topic to the destination cloud service. A data forwarding failure indicates that forwarding retries also fail. Valid values:

*   **true**: forwards error operation data.
*   **false**: forwards normal data instead of error operation data.

Default value: **false**.

CreateRuleAction.title: CreateRuleAction
CreateRuleAction.summary: Creates a rule action for a specified rule to forward processed data from a topic to another topic or a supported Alibaba Cloud service.
CreateRuleAction.description:
## Limits

*   Destination Alibaba Cloud services that are supported by the rules engine vary based on regions. For more information about the regions and destination cloud services that are supported by the rules engine, see [Regions and zones](~~85669~~).

*   You can create a maximum of 10 rule actions for each rule.

*   You can call this API operation to define rule actions to forward data to an IoT Platform topic, AMQP consumer group, or Alibaba Cloud service. The supported Alibaba Cloud services include Message Service (MNS), Function Compute, and Tablestore. If you need to forward data to ApsaraDB RDS, you must use the [IoT Platform console](https://iot.console.aliyun.com).

*   Each Alibaba Cloud account can run a maximum of 50 queries per second (QPS).

> RAM users of an Alibaba Cloud account share the quota of the account.
CreateRuleAction.requestParamsDescription:
**The configurations of the REPUBLISH type**| Parameter | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| topic | The destination topic. You can specify a Thing Specification Language (TSL) communication topic or a custom topic. You can forward data to the following downstream TSL communication topics: 

`/sys/${YourProductKey}/${YourDeviceName}/thing/service/property/set``/sys/${YourProductKey}/${YourDeviceName}/thing/service/${tsl.service.identifier}`Replace the **${tsl.service.identifier}** variable with a service identifier that is defined in the TSL model. |
| topicType | The type of the topic. Valid values: 

0: a downstream TSL communication topic. 

1: a custom topic. |
Examples****

```
A system topic: {"topic":"/sys/a1TXXXXXWSN/xxx_cache001/thing/service/property/set","topicType":0}
A custom topic: {"topic":"/a1TXXXXXWSN/xxx_cache001/user/update","topicType":1}
```

| regionName | The code of the region in which DataHub is deployed. Example: cn-shanghai. |
| role | The information about the RAM role. You can grant IoT Platform the access to DataHub by assigning a service role to IoT Platform. The syntax of a RAM role: 

`{"roleArn":"acs:ram::6541***:role/aliyuniotaccessingdatahubrole","roleName": "AliyunIOTAccessingDataHubRole"}`Replace `6541***` with your Alibaba Cloud ID. You can log on to the Alibaba Cloud Management Console and view the account ID on the Security Settings page.  

`AliyunIOTAccessingDataHubRole` indicates a service-linked role that is defined in RAM. This role is used to grant IoT Platform the access to DataHub. You can go to the RAM Roles page of the RAM console to manage RAM roles. |

schemaVals

BOOLEAN: Boolean.

CreateSharePromotionActivity.title: CreateSharePromotionActivity
CreateSharePromotionActivity.summary: Invoke this API to create a promotion activity for the Qianli Chuanyin sharing job.
CreateSharePromotionActivity.description:
## How-To

Because each device can join only one sharing job and can play back only the shared speech materials within that sharing job, the Qianli Chuanyin voice playback service provides a promotion activity feature that allows you to specify shared devices in a sharing job to broadcast speech materials from a promotion activity.

The configuration flow is as follows:

1. Call this API to create a promotion activity for all sharing jobs under the current instance.
2. Call the **QuerySharePromotionActivityAuditResult** API to query the review result of the promotion activity for a specified sharing job, and confirm that the promotion activity has passed the review.
3. Call the **CreateSharePromotionSpeechModel** API to add speech materials to the promotion activity.
4. Call the **AddDeviceToSharePromotion** API to add existing shared devices from the Qianli Chuanyin sharing job to the promotion activity.
5. Call the **ShareSpeechByCombination** API to play back the shared speech materials of the promotion activity.

For detailed configuration of sharing jobs, see [Use Shared Devices to Broadcast Shared Speech Materials](~~607661~~).

## QPS Limit

The maximum queries per second (QPS) for this API is 5 for each Alibaba Cloud account.

> All Resource Access Management (RAM) users under an Alibaba Cloud account share the quota of that Alibaba Cloud account.

- Custom speech material (default): Set this parameter to **custom**. When using custom speech material, you must specify both the speech material identity and text.

    - Monetary units: Set this parameter to **monetary_unit**. Supported content includes "fen", "jiao", and "yuan".  
    - Time units: Set this parameter to **time_unit**. Supported content includes "hour", "minute", "second", "month", "day", and "year".  
    - Unit time expressions: Set this parameter to **unit_time**. Supported content includes "per second", "per minute", "per hour", "per day", "per week", "per month", and "per year".

CreateSubscribeRelation.title: Create an MNS or AMQP server-side subscription
CreateSubscribeRelation.summary: Invoke this API to create an MNS or AMQP server-side subscription.
CreateSubscribeRelation.description:
## How-To  
Server-side subscriptions are available in two types:  
- **MNS subscription**: Subscribed messages are pushed to a queue in Message Service (MNS). Your server application receives device messages by listening to the MNS queue. For more information, see [Use MNS server-side subscription](~~68948~~). You can directly call this API to create an MNS subscription.  
- **AMQP subscription**: All subscribed messages under a product are pushed to your server through an AMQP channel. For more information, see [Configure AMQP server-side subscription](~~142376~~). Follow these steps to manage AMQP subscriptions:  
  1. Call [CreateConsumerGroup](~~170388~~) to create a consumer group and obtain the consumer group ID. In AMQP subscriptions, messages are pushed to the specified consumer group. Your AMQP client connects to IoT Platform using the consumer group ID to consume messages. For more information, see [AMQP client connection guide](~~142489~~).  
  2. Call this API to create an AMQP subscription.  
  3. (Optional) Call [CreateConsumerGroupSubscribeRelation](~~170354~~) to add a consumer group to the AMQP subscription. Call [DeleteConsumerGroupSubscribeRelation](~~170357~~) to remove a specific consumer group from multiple consumer groups in the AMQP subscription.  
  4. (Optional) While the AMQP subscription is running, call [QueryConsumerGroupStatus](~~170358~~) to query the status of a consumer group, including online client information, message consumption rate, number of accumulated messages, and the time of the most recent message consumption. Call [ResetConsumerGroupPosition](~~170355~~) to delete accumulated messages in the consumer group.

## Queries per second (QPS) limit  

The maximum queries per second (QPS) for this API per Alibaba Cloud account is 5.</props>

  > Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.

For more information, see [Create a queue](~~34417~~). | | regionName | The Alibaba Cloud Region code where the target Message Service is located, such as cn-shanghai. | | role | The authorization role information. Replace `5645*\**` with your Alibaba Cloud account ID. You can view your account ID on the Security Settings page of the console after logging in.
`AliyunIOTAccessingMNSRole` is a service role defined in Resource Access Management (RAM). It grants IoT Platform permission to access Message Service. DeleteDevice.summary: Deletes a device. You can also call this operation to delete the topological relationships between a gateway and the sub-devices that are connected to the gateway.
DeleteDevice.description:
*   When you call this operation with an Alibaba Cloud account, IoT Platform sends a verification code by text message to confirm your identity.
*   When you call this operation with a RAM user, IoT Platform does not send a verification code. To ensure device security, you can create custom permission policies to perform fine-grained permission management. For more information, see [Mapping of IoT Platform operations and RAM policies](~~47485~~) and [Custom permissions](~~47495~~).


**Warning**

*   After a device is deleted, the device ID (**IotId**) becomes invalid, and all other information associated with the device is deleted. In addition, you can no longer perform an operation on the device.
*   Before you delete a device in the IoT Platform console, make sure that the corresponding actual device is offline. Otherwise, after the device is deleted from IoT Platform, the actual device continues to initiate connection requests to IoT Platform. If the number of requests exceeds the upper limit, IoT Platform starts request throttling. In this case, access of other devices within your Alibaba Cloud account is affected.
*   After you delete a device, the certificate of the device becomes invalid and cannot be restored. Proceed with caution.

****

*   You must specify a value for the **IotId** parameter or values for the **ProductKey** and **DeviceName** parameters to identify a device.
*   If you specify a gateway and the number of sub-devices that belong to the gateway exceeds 2,000, you can call this operation to create a device job to delete the topological relationships in an asynchronous manner. The operation returns the **JobId** parameter.

## QPS limits

DeleteThingModel.title: Delete a specified feature from the Thing Specification Language model of a specified product
DeleteThingModel.summary: Invoke this API to delete a specified feature from the Thing Specification Language model of a specified product.
DeleteThingModel.description:
## How-To
- If the specified product has been published, you must first call the [CancelReleaseProduct](~~213875~~) API to cancel the product's publication before invoking this API to delete features from its Thing Specification Language model.
- You can also use this API to delete unpublished newly added feature definitions or custom modules in the Thing Specification Language model of the product.
- When calling this API, you must provide the **ProductKey** parameter and specify one of the following identifiers for the Thing Specification Language model: **FunctionBlockId**, **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, or **EventIdentifier.N**. The logic for deleting feature definitions from the Thing Specification Language model of the specified product is as follows:
    - If only **ProductKey** and **FunctionBlockId** are provided, the specified custom module in the Thing Specification Language model of the product is deleted.
    - If **ProductKey** and any of **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, or **EventIdentifier.N** are provided (without **FunctionBlockId**), the specified feature definitions within the default module of the product’s Thing Specification Language model are deleted. In this case, only the specified feature definitions that exist and have been passed in the request will be deleted. If none of the provided **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, or **EventIdentifier.N** values exist in the default module, the API call fails and returns an error code indicating that the feature definition does not exist.
    - If **ProductKey**, **FunctionBlockId**, and any of **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, or **EventIdentifier.N** are provided, the specified feature definitions within the custom module (identified by **FunctionBlockId**) of the product’s Thing Specification Language model are deleted. Only the specified feature definitions that exist and have been passed in the request will be deleted. If none of the provided **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, or **EventIdentifier.N** values exist in the custom module, the API call fails and returns an error code indicating that the feature definition does not exist.
    > You can pass up to 10 identifiers each for **PropertyIdentifier.N**, **ServiceIdentifier.N**, and **EventIdentifier.N**.

- After successfully deleting a feature from the Thing Specification Language model using this API, you must call the [PublishThingModel](~~150311~~) API to republish the product’s Thing Specification Language model. Otherwise, the deletion operation will not take effect.


## QPS Limit
The maximum queries per second (QPS) limit for this API is 5 per Alibaba Cloud account.  
> Resource Access Management (RAM) users share the quota of the Alibaba Cloud account.
